reviewCadence: At feature design, before release gates, and after every security-significant incident.

features.name: Account authentication
features.description: Password, passkey, MFA, session creation, recovery, and account onboarding flows.

features.name: Tenant and workspace authorization
features.description: Tenant, organization, workspace, role, and delegated actor authorization boundaries.

features.name: Browser mutating requests
features.description: Cookie-authenticated web requests, AJAX requests, CSRF protections, and browser metadata.

features.name: Web UI rendering
features.description: React rendering, reviewed HTML escape hatches, CSP, and clickjacking protections.

features.name: Cloud public access
features.description: Public share resolution, download URL creation, and public API signatures.

features.name: Billing and developer webhooks
features.description: Inbound Stripe webhooks and outbound developer webhook signing and replay handling.

features.name: Backoffice operations
features.description: Internal administrative mutation flows and privileged operator actions.

features.name: Audit, monitoring, and supply chain
features.description: Append-only audit evidence, detection coverage, dependency coverage, and secret scanning.

countermeasures.name: Authentication throttling and bot friction
countermeasures.description: IP, account, and pair-based rate limits, bot guard signals, and risk event recording.

countermeasures.name: MFA and step-up abuse controls
countermeasures.description: MFA rate limiting, failure auditing, recovery risk blocks, and step-up requirements for sensitive actions.

countermeasures.name: Workspace and tenant scope enforcement
countermeasures.description: Tenant, organization, workspace, delegated actor, role, and ownership boundaries.

countermeasures.name: CSRF, origin, and AJAX request guards
countermeasures.description: CSRF double-submit validation, Origin/Referer checks, Fetch Metadata rejection, and AJAX mutating headers.

countermeasures.name: Security headers and clickjacking controls
countermeasures.description: CSP frame-ancestors, X-Frame-Options, strict content type, referrer, permissions, and cross-origin headers.

countermeasures.name: Reviewed HTML rendering guardrails
countermeasures.description: SafeHtml, VerifiedHtml, and repository checks that block risky DOM sinks and JSONP.

countermeasures.name: Public API and share abuse controls
countermeasures.description: HMAC request signatures, nonce and timestamp validation, public share rate limits, clean-scan checks, and denial audit.

countermeasures.name: Webhook authenticity and replay controls
countermeasures.description: Raw payload signature verification, payload hashing, duplicate handling, fresh outbound signatures, and replay status gates.

countermeasures.name: Backoffice privileged action gates
countermeasures.description: Permission headers, active operator grants, idempotency keys, and strong confirmation gates.

countermeasures.name: Audit immutability
countermeasures.description: Hash-bearing audit events with mutation-prevention triggers in product schemas.

countermeasures.name: Supply chain and secret scanning
countermeasures.description: Repository checks for secrets, dependency coverage, SBOM evidence, container checks, and license boundaries.

abuseCases.attack: An attacker automates credential stuffing, password spraying, registration abuse, or bot-driven authentication probes.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP A2 Broken Authentication; OWASP Automated Threats

abuseCases.attack: An attacker brute-forces MFA, abuses recovery paths, or keeps retrying failed step-up flows to take over an account.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP Multifactor Authentication; OWASP A2 Broken Authentication

abuseCases.attack: An authenticated actor changes tenant, organization, workspace, or object identifiers to access or mutate another customer's resources.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP A5 Broken Access Control; OWASP IDOR

includes: all workspace IDs must belong to the requested scope

abuseCases.attack: An attacker triggers cookie-authenticated mutations through forged browser requests, cross-site forms, or weak AJAX request handling.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP CSRF Prevention; OWASP AJAX Security

abuseCases.attack: An attacker frames privileged UI, clickjacks account actions, or exploits missing browser hardening headers.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP Clickjacking Defense; OWASP A6 Security Misconfiguration

abuseCases.attack: An attacker turns AJAX-controlled data or generated markup into DOM XSS through unsafe HTML sinks, string execution, or JSONP.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP A7 Cross-Site Scripting; OWASP AJAX Security

includes: Do not evaluate AJAX-controlled data as code.

abuseCases.attack: An attacker tampers with public API requests, replays signed calls, or automates public share downloads to abuse bandwidth and data access.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP API Security; OWASP Denial of Service

abuseCases.attack: An attacker sends fake, tampered, stale, or duplicate webhook payloads to trigger billing or developer-side effects.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP Webhook Security; OWASP A5 Broken Access Control

abuseCases.attack: A compromised, confused, or overprivileged operator attempts irreversible backoffice mutations without the right role, grant, idempotency, or confirmation context.
An attacker alters or deletes audit evidence to hide account, cloud, billing, or administrative abuse.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP A10 Insufficient Logging and Monitoring

abuseCases.attack: An attacker exploits leaked secrets, unknown vulnerable dependencies, missing SBOM evidence, or weak container/dependency hygiene.
abuseCases.referential: OWASP A9 Vulnerable Components; OWASP Software Supply Chain Security
